headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0088 — SMTO can't tell if your Microsoft 365 change was made

html:
SMTO-SKL-0088 — SMTO can't tell if your Microsoft 365 change was made

GUID: a79aab6f-361b-5689-aec1-b08ed5b9a888
Slug: microsoft365-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO sent a change to Microsoft, such as moving, flagging or deleting an email or editing a contact, but couldn't confirm the result. It may already be done, so SMTO won't repeat it on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: open Outlook with the same Microsoft account and find the email, folder or contact SMTO was changing. Microsoft may have made the change even though SMTO never got the reply.
  2. Look for the specific change, for example the email in its new folder, the flag, the deleted item in Deleted Items, or the new contact. Seeing the result tells you whether anything still needs to be done.
  3. Only if the change is missing, ask SMTO to make it again and approve it when asked. Repeating a change that already happened could create a duplicate or act on the wrong item.

What success looks like

  • Outlook shows the change exactly once, as you intended.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what you asked for and when, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep repeating the request until you've checked Outlook.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 write (mail draft, move, copy, flag, read state, delete, attachment, mail/contact folder or calendar container, or contact change) lost reliable acknowledgement: network failure, 500/502/503/504, unexpected success status, unreadable response, or a create that returned no ID; any PATCH read-back did not prove the change.

What this means

  • Graph mutation transport, unexpected success status or unreadable acknowledgement cannot establish a reliable completed write result. Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.

Why this can happen

  • Graph mutation transport, unexpected success status or unreadable acknowledgement cannot establish a reliable completed write result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation family, exact resource and retained request identifiers.

How to fix it

  • Check whether your action already happened: read the exact resource under the same account_ref (mail_read_message, contact_read, the folder's _get operation, or a search for a create) and compare it with the intended change. Only issue a new write after confirming the change is absent; do not replay the original mutation.
  • Reconcile the exact original operation and resource from retained request evidence before issuing another write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Provider state establishes the actual outcome before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
